title: Set up registered agent
summary: Every state of incorporation requires a registered agent for legal documents — pick a service and designate it online.

parts.title: Choose registered agent service
parts.guidance: Compare registered-agent services for the company’s formation and qualification states. Check the designation details, consent process, legal-notice handling, account access and renewal charges. Distinguish service of legal papers from ordinary mail forwarding. Choose a provider that covers the required states and gives the company a reliable path for urgent notices before approving the purchase.

parts.title: Sign up online and designate the agent
parts.guidance: Create the company account for the purchased service and obtain the exact agent name and address required in the state record. Check whether appointment or replacement needs a separate filing. Complete the designation and fees through the entity’s authorized filing process. Verify both provider activation and registry acceptance, then test notice routing to the company’s responsible contact.

verify.how: The agent's name and Delaware address appear on the entity's record in the Division of Corporations entity search.

parts.title: Designate the agent in each additional registered state
parts.guidance: Check the agent requirements and provider coverage in each additional registration state. Use that state’s correct agent details and appointment process, with the authorized filer approving submission. Verify the accepted designation and route notices to the appropriate company contact. A service subscription elsewhere does not establish an appointment in this state.

parts.title: Change the Delaware registered agent (Certificate of Change, $50)
parts.guidance: If the Delaware agent is being replaced, have the board adopt the change resolution 8 Del. C. § 133 requires and prepare the certificate of change for the Division of Corporations, with the new agent's consent on record (law rule us-de.registered-agent-change). The state filing fee is $50 on the Division's fee schedule; commercial agents usually prepare and submit the certificate as part of their onboarding. Confirm acceptance and that the entity search shows the new agent before cancelling the old service.

cost.note: Domestic corporation 'Change of Agent/Office' state filing fee on the Division of Corporations fee schedule revised August 1, 2026. Conditional step — excluded from the default-flow fee headline by construction.

parts.title: Designate or change the California agent for service of process (Statement of Information)
parts.guidance: California corporations name their agent for service of process in the Statement of Information (Form SI-550, $25 filing fee — law rule us-ca.statement-of-information), filed through bizfile Online within 90 days of registration and annually after. To change the agent, file a new statement with the replacement agent's details; an entity may name an individual with a California street address or a registered corporate agent. Verify the updated agent appears on the entity's record in Business Search.

references.title: CA SOS — agents for service of process

parts.title: Update the New York registered agent or process address (Certificate of Change, $30)
parts.guidance: New York names the Secretary of State as every corporation's agent for service of process; a separate registered agent is optional. To change the registered agent or the address where the Secretary of State forwards process, file a Certificate of Change with the Department of State for a $30 fee — Business Corporation Law § 1309-A for a foreign corporation (the Delaware-default company qualifying in New York), § 805-A for a domestic New York corporation (law rule us-ny.registered-agent-change); some address updates can instead ride the $9 biennial statement. Keep the forwarding address current — it is where lawsuits arrive.

cost.note: Certificate of Change under BCL § 805-A(a) / § 1309-A(b) on the Department of State fee schedule. Conditional step — excluded from the default-flow fee headline by construction.

parts.title: File Texas Form 401 to change the registered agent or office ($15)
parts.guidance: Texas entities change the registered agent or registered office by filing Form 401 (Statement of Change of Registered Office/Agent) with the Secretary of State; the fee is $15 for a for-profit entity, and the named agent must have consented, with a filed consent costing a further $15 if recorded (law rule us-tx.registered-agent-change). Submit through SOSDirect/SOSUpload or by mail, and confirm the record shows the new agent before cancelling the old one.

cost.note: Form 401 filing fee for a change of registered office/agent ($5 for nonprofit corporations and cooperative associations), per the form instructions. Conditional step — excluded from the default-flow fee headline by construction.

parts.title: Appoint or change the Wyoming registered agent ($5)
parts.guidance: Wyoming entities change to a new registered agent with the Secretary of State's Appointment of New Registered Agent and Office form, which carries the agent's signed Consent to Appointment and certifies compliance with W.S. 17-28-101 through 17-28-111 (law rule us-wy.registered-agent-change). The filing fee is $5, the form is mail-only, and processing can take up to 15 business days — plan agent switches ahead of any filing that depends on the new agent.

cost.note: Appointment of New Registered Agent and Office filing fee, per the form checklist. Conditional step — excluded from the default-flow fee headline by construction.

parts.title: Change the Florida registered agent ($35)
parts.guidance: Florida corporations change the registered agent or registered office with the Division of Corporations for a $35 fee (law rule us-fl.registered-agent-change), using the Sunbiz change filing; at registration the $35 agent-designation fee is paid alongside the $35 filing fee. The incoming agent accepts the appointment on the filing. Confirm the Sunbiz record shows the new agent before cancelling the old service.

cost.note: 'Change of Registered Agent' on the Division of Corporations corporate fee schedule. Conditional step — excluded from the default-flow fee headline by construction.

metadata.supportReason: Registered agent services have no public signup API — the designation is an online form; provider comparison is agent work.

geoNotes.summary: No agent industry: the analog is the registered office itself — declared at (or within 30 days of) incorporation via form INC-22 to the MCA (fronted by NSWS), with the company name displayed at the premises.

The analog is the registered office: since the 2023 ECCT Act it must be an 'appropriate address' where documents reliably reach the company (PO boxes alone are out), plus a registered email — agent-provided addresses remain fine.

No registered-agent concept: the GmbH registers an inländische Geschäftsanschrift (domestic business address) in the Handelsregister where service of process is valid — keep it current via the notary when you move.

The analog is the siège social declared through the guichet unique: it can be the founder's home or a domiciliation company — the latter must hold a prefectural agrément — and changing it is a formal statuts amendment.

No registered-agent industry: the company's sede (registered office) is declared at formation in the commercial registry and service of process reaches the company there — keep it current with an online registry filing.

No registered-agent industry: the registered office address is declared in the articles filed with Corporations Canada (or the provincial registry) and must stay current — documents are served on the corporation there.
